scope: Ordered native body/contact TGS frame from fresh caller-supplied manifolds and two conflict-free colors; no collision generation or changing topology
tolerance_reason: Existing Coulomb/body f32 tolerances remain unchanged for composed one-frame checkpoints. IDs, padding, copied fields, uniforms and inactive storage stay exact.
preconditions: Fresh caller-supplied native contact manifolds with valid fixed color order; no recycled links or hubs
Two solved colors with disjoint velocity writers within each color, including static slots; colors may share bodies sequentially
Finite unit rotations, positive timestep, matching native batch/substep/PGS uniforms
All dynamic bodies remain awake; no sleeping or scene culling
The native ContactPlan bound is supplied in device storage and does not exceed the declared launch capacity; standalone fixtures declare its live count.
invariants: Generated kernels update world masses, initialize body state, prepare contacts and apply gravity before warmstart/solve/integrate/finalize in Rust order
At least one biased PGS iteration per substep even when configured count is zero; friction mode and impulse scaling follow native uniforms
Caller-owned buffers stay resident; no CPU physics or intermediate readback
Fixed body velocities and poses are invariant; final rotations remain normalized and impulses obey unilateral/Coulomb bounds
Every untouched word and integer field remains exact
Every contact invocation reads the device plan bound before dereferencing contact or body storage; padded invocations preserve every guard word.
outside_scope: Frame-to-frame contact recycling and changing topology
General graph coloring/bucket/hub composition and shared static slots within one color
Rigid-body joints, twist friction and fused/tail optimizations
Long-run stability qualification and the retained zero-distance numerical boundary
Production public backend selection and Ascend vendor execution
